text.p: These are the main stories in Lithuanian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Two students of the Vilnius arts academy, Jolanta Rimkute and Ieva Sheviakovaite, were awarded the golden button prize at the international fashion festival, In Vogue Vilnius'97.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas intends to pay attention to the development of economic co-operation with Japan during his first official visit to the country on May 12-15.

- The April issue of The Banker magazine used incorrect information on macroeconomic data about Lithuania saying that inflation in the country last year was 26 percent instead of 13.1 and GDP growth was 1.5 percent instead of 3.6 percent.

- State-run Lithuanian Agricultural bank, slated for privatisation, wants to get rid of its bad loans and become attractive to investors, chairman Vaclovas Litvinas said in an interview to the newspaper.
- Five years have passed since agreement on bilateral relations between Lithuania and Russia, signed in July 1991, came into force.
- The ferry Palanga of the Lithuanian Sea Shipping company departed from Klaipeda port to Ahus in Sweden on Sunday. A regular service will be opened in June to run twice a week.
- Taiwanese and Lithuanian economic relations will become more intensive in the future, said Taiwan's deputy minister fr foreign affairs Chien Jen Chenis.
- One of the biggest electronics producers, Vilniaus Vingis, intends to decide on a 16 million litas share capital boost in its shareholders meeting on May 31.
- The textile industry produced 23.6 million square metres of materials in the first quarter of 1997. Last year the industry produced 78.3 million square metres.
